column2: Archicad 29 with a built-in AI assistant
column3: Graphisoft releases Archicad 29 with the AI assistant announced in January, still in beta: it answers questions about the software and the model and integrates with the AI Visualizer. The full commercial version is expected in 2026.

column2: Czech Republic: BIM law, mandatory from 2027
column3: Under the new BIM law, from 1 January 2027 public projects above CZK 135 million (about €5.4 million) must use BIM for the whole life cycle of the building, from design to demolition. The law also introduces a national data standard for construction.

column2: EU BIM Task Group: a balanced European approach to BIM in procurement
column3: The EU BIM Task Group publishes a position paper on the role of BIM in public procurement: better value for public money, transparency and more sustainable works, with common rules but without imposing the same timing on everyone.

column2: Germany: BIM models become official project documents
column3: The federal government approves the «Infrastruktur-Zukunftsgesetz» bill to speed up infrastructure: project approval procedures become fully digital and BIM models are recognised as official documents. The text now goes to Parliament.

column2: IFC 5: first alpha version released
column3: buildingSMART publishes the alpha version of IFC 5, the new generation of the open format for exchanging BIM models: easier to implement, designed for the web and released in modules, starting from the common core. A report on the core consultation follows in October.

column2: Ireland: the BIM mandate extends to projects above €20 million
column3: A new step of the BIM mandate in Irish public procurement: after projects above €100 million, from June 2025 design teams must also apply it above €20 million; for contractors and suppliers the deadline is the end of the year.

column2: Shanghai: new rules for delivering BIM models for review
column3: Shanghai's construction commission sets how detailed-design BIM models used in assisted design review must be modelled and delivered in IFC format. The rules apply from 15 June 2025, together with the update of automated checking.

column2: Japan: design review with BIM begins
column3: From 1 April, building permits can go through «BIM drawing review»: drawings produced from a BIM model are checked with simplified consistency checks, while the IFC file accompanies the application as a reference. The ministry aims to review IFC data directly from spring 2029.

column2: OICE report: BIM tenders grow by 80% in 2025
column3: According to the ninth OICE report, in 2025 tenders with BIM grew by 80.7% in number and 151% in value, reaching 27% of engineering and architecture service tenders in Italy. But only one tender in three includes the information requirements.

column2: Dubai: BIM becomes mandatory for permits of large buildings
column3: From January 2024 Dubai Municipality requires BIM models in IFC format for building permits of the tallest buildings and large complexes, special buildings such as hospitals and universities, and public projects.

column2: Ireland: BIM mandate starts in public works
column3: From 1 January 2024 BIM requirements enter the national framework for public works (CWMF): first step for design teams on projects above €100 million, then gradual extension to lower thresholds and to contractors and suppliers.

column2: IDS 1.0: information requirements become automatically checkable
column3: buildingSMART International approves the Information Delivery Specification (IDS) 1.0 as a final standard: a machine-readable file stating which information an IFC model must contain and allowing it to be checked automatically, in line with ISO 19650.

column2: Nemetschek buys GoCanvas for over $700 million
column3: The Nemetschek group (Allplan, Graphisoft, Bluebeam) announces the acquisition of US company GoCanvas, software for digitalising site and field work, for about 11.5 times its 2023 recurring revenue. The deal closes on 1 July.

column2: ISO 7817-1: level of information need becomes an ISO standard
column3: ISO 7817-1:2024 on «level of information need» is published: concepts and principles to state consistently how much and which information, geometric and non-geometric, is needed at each stage. In Europe it replaces EN 17412-1:2020.

column2: Malaysia: BIM mandatory above RM10 million, also for roads and sewers
column3: The BIM mandate for public and private projects from RM10 million upwards extends to the design and construction of roads and sewer networks. The deputy minister of works links it to the Jalan Masjid India sinkhole: mapping underground utilities well reduces clashes and risks.

column2: openBIM Awards 2024 presented in Marrakech
column3: At the buildingSMART International Summit, held with the CIB W78 conference, the best openBIM projects of the year are awarded after presentations by 22 finalists. Jack Cheng's group at HKUST in Hong Kong wins the student research category.

column2: Autodesk bets on «outcome-based BIM»
column3: At Autodesk University, Autodesk connects Forma to Autodesk Docs, its project data repository, relaunches the AEC Data Model API for working with data at a granular level and presents Autodesk Assistant in beta, which answers questions about specifications in Autodesk Construction Cloud.

column2: Procurement corrective decree: government raises the BIM threshold to €2 million
column3: The Italian Council of Ministers approves the draft corrective decree to the Public Contracts Code: from 1 January 2025 the digital information management obligation applies to works above €2 million instead of €1 million, with its own threshold for works on cultural heritage. The text then goes to the Unified Conference and the Council of State.

column2: Germany: the strategy to bring BIM to all federal buildings
column3: The BIM steering group of the building and defence ministries publishes the implementation strategy of the BIM Masterplan for federal buildings: project organisation, use cases, BIM manual and gradual steps towards the next levels of the mandate.

column2: New Public Contracts Code: digital information management becomes mandatory
column3: Italian Legislative Decree 36/2023 introduces in article 43 the obligation for contracting authorities to adopt digital information management methods and tools for construction from 1 January 2025; Annex I.9 sets out the organisational act, training, roles and the common data environment.

column2: Japan: BIM/CIM mandatory in national public works
column3: From fiscal year 2023 the infrastructure ministry applies BIM/CIM in principle to all civil engineering assignments and works it manages directly, except small ones: data sharing by the client and 3D models according to purpose.

column2: Autodesk launches Forma, the cloud for building design
column3: Autodesk presents the first features of Forma, the successor of Spacemaker: context modelling, early-stage design, environmental analysis and AI-based automation, with a direct link to Revit. It is included in the AEC Collection.

column2: Spain: BIM Plan for public procurement approved
column3: The Council of Ministers approves the plan to introduce BIM in the State's public construction contracts, with a progressive timetable based on BIM level and contract value. The plan is published in the Official Gazette with Order PCM/818/2023 of 18 July.

column2: openBIM Awards 2023 presented in Lillestrøm
column3: At the buildingSMART International Summit in Norway, ten winners and five special mentions are announced. Kasimir Forth of TU Munich wins two awards, in the student research and sustainability categories.

column2: Singapore: the timetable for moving to CORENET X
column3: Singapore's authorities set the steps for bringing building submissions onto the new CORENET X platform, with BIM models in the open IFC+SG format: first a voluntary phase, then the mandate for new projects, later postponed and phased by size.

column2: Russia: information model mandatory for state-funded works
column3: Government decree no. 331 of 5 March 2021 enters into force: for state-funded construction, the information model of the asset becomes mandatory, excluding defence and security facilities. The extension to the whole sector was later postponed several times.

column2: ISO 19650-4: rules for information exchange
column3: The fourth part of the ISO 19650 series is published, dedicated to information exchange: how to decide, at each delivery, whether the information shared in the common data environment is adequate and can be approved. CEN adopts it in the autumn.

column2: United States: the National BIM Program is born
column3: The National Institute of Building Sciences launches the US National BIM Program, aiming to digitalise design, construction and operation: a common strategy between the federal government and the private sector, in a country without a national BIM mandate.

column2: Germany: the federal government's BIM portal opens
column3: Ministers Wissing and Geywitz open the federal BIM-Portal to the public: a single platform with information requirement templates, object classes and common properties for all federal public works, after an internal pilot phase.

column2: openBIM Awards 2022 presented in Montréal
column3: At the buildingSMART International Summit in Montréal, held with the Canadian national conference, 9 projects are awarded and 3 special mentions given, chosen from 121 entries and 21 finalists.

column2: IFC 4.3 passes the ISO vote as a draft international standard
column3: IFC 4.3, the version of the open format extended to roads, railways, bridges and ports, passes the ISO draft international standard stage with 22 votes in favour and one against. A final review stage is needed before publication as the new ISO 16739.

column2: Brazil: first phase of the federal BIM mandate begins
column3: From 1 January 2021 BIM is mandatory in architecture and engineering design for new works and major refurbishments of some federal bodies, starting with pilot programmes of the defence and infrastructure ministries. The next phases come in 2024 and 2028.

column2: Italian recovery plan: guidelines for the feasibility design
column3: The Italian Higher Council of Public Works unanimously approves the guidelines on the technical and economic feasibility design of PNRR and PNC works: minimum content of the design and of the design brief, including the digital information models required in design-and-build contracts.

column2: United Kingdom: from BIM Level 2 to the information management mandate
column3: The Infrastructure and Projects Authority publishes the 2030 roadmap «Transforming Infrastructure Performance»: the old 2011 BIM Level 2 mandate gives way to an Information Management Mandate, applied through the UK BIM Framework and the ISO 19650 series.

column2: Germany: the BIM Masterplan for federal buildings
column3: The federal government publishes the Masterplan BIM für Bundesbauten: three levels of gradual introduction of BIM for the whole life cycle of state buildings, with common use cases. It becomes binding with a decree of January 2022.

column2: The first BIM mandate starts: complex works above €100 million
column3: With Ministerial Decree 560/2017 the timetable of the BIM mandate in Italian public procurement begins: from 1 January 2019 for complex works from €100 million upwards, then lower thresholds every year until 2025.

column2: United Kingdom: the UK BIM Framework is launched
column3: At Digital Construction Week, the UK BIM Alliance, BSI and the Centre for Digital Built Britain launch the UK BIM Framework, which replaces «BIM Level 2» and brings the ISO 19650 series into British practice, with a website of free guidance.

column2: UNI/PdR 74:2019: the BIM management system is born
column3: UNI publishes the reference practice on the requirements of organisations' BIM management system (SGBIM), certifiable like a quality system. In 2026 it is replaced by UNI 11337-8.

column2: Germany: BIM Deutschland, the national BIM centre, starts
column3: BIM Deutschland starts, the national centre for the digitalisation of construction set up by the transport and building ministries: a single reference point for introducing BIM in a coordinated way in infrastructure and public buildings.

column2: ISO 19650-5: information security in BIM
column3: ISO 19650-5 is published, dedicated to security-minded information management: how to protect sensitive data of buildings and infrastructure, for example those of strategic assets, when models are shared.

column2: ISO 19650-3: information management in the operational phase
column3: The third part of ISO 19650 is published, on information management during the operation and maintenance of built assets: the operator's information requirements and the asset information model.

column2: Autodesk buys Spacemaker for $240 million
column3: Autodesk announces the acquisition of Norwegian company Spacemaker, which uses artificial intelligence to generate and evaluate site and building layout options in minutes. This will lead, in 2023, to Autodesk Forma.

column2: Singapore: BIM mandatory for building submissions above 5,000 m²
column3: Final step of the plan of Singapore's building authority: from 1 July 2015 all new buildings above 5,000 m² must make building submissions with BIM models, after the 20,000 m² thresholds of 2013 and 2014.

column2: Procurement Code 2016: BIM enters the law
column3: Italy's new Public Contracts Code (Legislative Decree 50/2016) allows contracting authorities to require electronic modelling methods and tools for new works and works on existing buildings, especially complex works, and refers to a ministerial decree for the timing and terms of the mandate.
